baseline.canonical_rules: Two countries repeatedly bargain over a divisible allocation. Each round one proposer offers terms; the responder accepts immediately or rejects and the game continues, with discounted continuation payoffs.
baseline.proposer_protocol: Candidate benchmark: alternating offers A,B,A,B in successive rounds. Whether fixed or alternating proposer best matches the substantive puzzle requires human approval; do not silently substitute a different game.
baseline.rejection_transition: Rejecting an offer advances to the next round without an automatic attack or war, preserving the conventional bargaining benchmark. War/outside options would require a separately justified change.
baseline.discounting: A and B discount next-round values with fixed factors delta_A and delta_B strictly between zero and one; state dependence enters only through the selected holiday primitive.
baseline.information: Complete information about preferences, discount factors, calendar and past offers; the four-state calendar is announced and perfectly anticipated.
baseline.baseline_source_status: Conventional infinite-horizon bargaining benchmark: exact original scholarly reference and equilibrium assumptions still require full-text verification.

innovation.one_sentence_change: Allow one conventional bargaining payoff or rejection-cost primitive to depend on a publicly known four-state holiday calendar, leaving the rest of the repeated ultimatum game unchanged.
innovation.payoff_or_transition_affected: Candidate single change: holiday_state shifts a player's cost of rejecting and continuing to the next bargaining round. The sign, symmetry and interpretation are not yet identified.

mechanism.candidate_literature_gap: The preliminary screened literature examines holiday-associated violence in terrorism, insurgency, communal riots and ceasefires; how strategic anticipation affects interstate bargaining timing remains a candidate, not established, research gap.
mechanism.mechanism: Players anticipate calendar-dependent continuation costs, possibly changing acceptance thresholds, offers, or the timing of rejected bargains. Whether any military attack behavior follows requires an additional, explicitly justified outcome link.
mechanism.null_case: If holiday shifts are symmetric, offset by offers, or do not change continuation incentives, observable conflict timing may be unchanged despite a calendar state.
mechanism.rival_explanation: Operational readiness, religious norms, media reporting, and event-coding seasonality could explain apparent holiday timing without bargaining effects.

proof_plan.solution_concept: Find and characterize appropriate subgame-perfect equilibrium or a clearly restricted stationary or calendar-periodic Markov-perfect equilibrium; justify any equilibrium selection.
proof_plan.equilibrium_conditions: Derive Bellman/continuation-value equations for each holiday state, best responses, participation and acceptance thresholds; identify discount and cost domains with valid equilibria.
proof_plan.off_path_requirements: Verify rejected-offer continuation, deviations at each calendar state, optimality of offers and acceptance thresholds, and any threatened war/outside-option actions if later introduced.
proof_plan.benchmark_recovery: Set holiday-dependent cost variation to zero and recover the published benchmark bargaining equilibrium and its interpretation before deriving any new effects.

source_caveats: Current Holy Days literature stage was approved only as a preliminary abstract/entry screening, not a full-text novelty review.
The baseline repeated bargaining game needs a verified canonical scholarly reference and a precise choice between fixed versus alternating proposer.
This is a blueprint, not an equilibrium proof or an established interstate holiday effect.
